# fin.dated_rates

An immutable date-banded rate table, such as a teaser rate that reverts.

## Overview

`fin.dated_rates` is owned by the [`fin`](../stdlib/fin.md) module (see [Rate and charge
tables](../stdlib/fin.md#rate-and-charge-tables) for what the four tables share). It is built from a one-line text
form or from band records:

| text form | band record |
| --- | --- |
| `"2026-01-01:0.04, 2026-07-01:0.02"` — each band from a date to the next | `{from: date, rate}` |

<a id="accrue"></a>
### `accrue(principal, start, end, convention, scale, mode) -> decimal`

Answer the interest on `principal` from `start` to `end`, the rate changing at band dates.

```go
fin := import("fin")
dr := fin.dated_rates("2026-01-01:0.04, 2026-07-01:0.02")
dr.accrue(10000, d"2026-01-01", d"2027-01-01", "ACT/365F", 2, "half_even")   // => 299.18d — 198.36 + 100.82
```

<a id="accrue_parts"></a>
### `accrue_parts(principal, start, end, convention, scale, mode) -> array`

Answer each stretch of the accrual, as `[{start, end, rate, amount}]`; see [`accrue`](#accrue).

<a id="apply"></a>
### `apply(amount, on, scale, mode) -> decimal` / `apply(amount, on, fallback, scale, mode) -> decimal`

Answer `amount` × the rate in force on `on`, rounded once.

<a id="at"></a>
### `at(on[, fallback]) -> decimal`

Answer the rate in force on the date `on`; `fallback` answers **only** a date before the first band.

```go
fin := import("fin")
dr := fin.dated_rates("2026-01-01:0.04, 2026-07-01:0.02")
dr.at(d"2025-12-31")                            // Error: invalid_value: (at) no band covers the argument
dr.at(d"2025-12-31", 0.05d)                     // => 0.05d — the fallback, before the first band only
```

<a id="bands"></a>
### `bands() -> array`

Answer the bands as records in constructor shape, so the table rebuilds from them: `fin.dated_rates(t.bands()) == t`.

<a id="copy"></a>
### `copy() -> fin.dated_rates`

Answer the table itself — it is immutable.
